choices.text: It crumbles away all by itself, with nothing wearing it
People quietly carry the rock away at night
Moving water and wind wear the rock away, loosening and carrying bits off
The sea pushes the whole cliff backwards in one go

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Rocks crumble on their own, with nothing doing the wearing. In fact moving water and wind do the wearing: waves loosen bits of rock and currents carry them away.
questions.misconception: Rocks crumble on their own, with nothing doing the wearing.
questions.prompt: Why does a coastal cliff get smaller over time?

choices.text: It glues them back onto the cliff
It carries them away along the coast
It turns them back into hard rock
It hides them under the cliff

questions.explanation: The current is moving water: once waves loosen a bit of rock, the current carries it away, which is why the cliff gets smaller.
questions.prompt: What does a sea current do to loose bits of rock at a cliff?

questions.answer: Moving water (waves batter and loosen the rock, currents carry loose bits away) and wind (moving air wears at the rock and helps carry small bits away).
questions.explanation: Both movers must be named with their jobs: waves loosen, currents carry, and wind wears and carries. Rock never wears itself away.
questions.prompt: Name two movers that wear rock away at the coast, and say what each one does.

questions.answer: On a calm day there is little moving water or wind, so almost no wearing happens. In stormy weather strong waves batter the cliff and strong winds wear at it, loosening bits that currents then carry away.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that the wearing needs a mover: calm weather means weak movers and little change, stormy weather means strong movers and faster erosion.
questions.prompt: A cliff looks exactly the same on a calm, still day but smaller after a stormy month. Explain why.

choices.text: The waves batter the cliff and loosen bits of rock
The wind carries the whole cliff away
The rock crumbles before any wave arrives
The current builds a new cliff

questions.explanation: Erosion at the cliff starts with the battering: wave after wave cracks the rock and loosens bits, which are then carried away.
questions.prompt: What happens first when waves erode a cliff?

subject: geography
title: Erosion: wind and water wear rock away
